source.title: Transformers on Markov Data: Constant Depth Suffices
source.authors: Nived Rajaraman; Marco Bondaschi; K. Ramchandran; Michael Gastpar; A. Makkuva

page_placements.theme: Generalised and higher-order induction in toy models and theory

record.file_problem: The full paper is present. Some mathematical notation is flattened or garbled, but the relevant results are readable.
record.tranche_reason: The paper tests induction-head representation and related limits through constructions, conditional theoretical bounds, and a different empirical attention measurement; it is not a reproduction of the original training-dynamics method.
record.gate_note: Figure 4 reports training trajectories for test-loss gap from the optimum, but does not measure induction-head formation, loss falling with token index, or a bump in training loss. It is recorded under fits_no_version, not as evidence for V2. The paper also reports a one-layer conditional-k-gram lower bound, which does not test the two-or-more-layer induction-head versions. Results cited from other studies are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: Mostly a representation-theory paper on Markov data. Only Figure 8 and Theorem 4.1 bear on V1. Figure 8 shows the first layer of a trained 2-layer, 1-head attention-only model is a previous-token head. Theorem 4.1 shows a previous-token layer composed with a matching layer implements the order-1 induction mechanism. No training-dynamics, scale or few-shot measurements.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors also report empirically that 2- and 3-layer, 1-head transformers learn order-4 and order-8 Markov chains, more than previously anticipated. They prove a 1-layer lower bound and conditional lower bounds: Ω(log k) layers or Ω(k) heads for attention-only kth-order induction heads. They name gradient-descent learning dynamics as future work.
record.recipe_differences: This is a representation-power study on Markov data, not a reproduction of the original induction-head training-dynamics measurements. It combines theoretical constructions and bounds with Markov-source training experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: The representational bounds depend on depth and head count and require Assumption 6.2. The empirical results vary Markov order and transformer depth; the text also notes that attention-pattern variance may depend on the iteration budget.

fits_no_version.finding: 2- and 3-layer, 1-head GPT-2-style transformers (with MLPs and layer norm) reach near-optimal test loss on order-4 and order-8 Markov data. That exceeds the conditional limits on attention-only kth-order induction heads.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Non-linearities let shallow single-head transformers implement higher-order (long-prefix) induction heads beyond attention-only size limits.

fits_no_version.finding: Attention-only transformers need about log2(k) layers, or about k first-layer heads, to realize a kth-order induction head when earlier layers use position-only attention. Constructions match these orders.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Higher-order induction heads have depth/head-count requirements in attention-only transformers.

fits_no_version.finding: A 3-layer, 1-head transformer with layer normalization can represent conditional k-grams for any k.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Layer normalization enables constant-depth kth-order induction heads.

fits_no_version.finding: In 2-layer, k-head attention-only models (k=2,3), first-layer heads attend to fixed earlier offsets, with some input-dependent variance (Appendix G, Figs 11 and 15).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Trained multi-head first layers implement fixed-offset heads for higher-order induction.

record.problems: The training experiments use randomly sampled Markov sources and report averages over 3 runs; numerical trajectories are shown only in plots. The empirical head measurement described in the text is for one trained order-1 model and covers only its first-layer attention. The lower bounds are conditional on Assumption 6.2.
record.rows_left_out: No reported results meeting the row criteria were left out.

untested.parts: Second-layer matching and copying in trained models, and composition between the two layers in trained weights. Whether training generally finds the mechanism.
All of it. There is no formation timing, token-index ICL measure or loss bump.
All of it; no large models.
All of it. Markov order is varied, but induction-head formation is not measured as a function of it.

missing.what: First-layer attention patterns of 2-layer, 2-head and 3-head attention-only models trained on order-2 and order-3 Markov data. Heads attend to fixed earlier offsets, with some variance.
Lower bound for 1-layer transformers computing conditional 3-grams: 2pH+dp+2 ≥ T/3.

record.verdict_notes: Most rows concern kth-order (long-prefix) induction heads, a generalisation not named by any version; they were relinked to none. The only V1 evidence is one trained order-1 attention-only model's previous-token first layer plus an existence construction, so the support is thin.

versions.untested_parts: The paper gives constructions and conditional representation bounds, and measures a first-layer previous-token attention pattern in one trained model. It does not establish that training generally produces the complete composed mechanism in small attention-only models.
No measurement of induction-head formation over training, its timing relative to token-index in-context learning, or a bump in the training-loss curve.
No large transformers or measurement of the share of their in-context learning carried by induction heads.
No sweep across model families, modalities, or independently trained runs to test universality.

The experiments use Markov sources and vary order and architecture, but do not compare data or training setups to test how those properties affect induction formation or persistence of in-context learning.
No few-shot task-learning test or comparison of induction heads with other mechanisms for carrying few-shot learning.
No measurement of multiple sub-steps or overlapping transitions in induction-head formation.

rows.subject: 2-layer, 1-head attention-only transformer
rows.operation_detail: Constructed an attention-only transformer representing the conditional 1-gram model using a previous-token attention layer followed by a matching-token attention layer.
rows.measure: Representation of the conditional 1-gram model by the specified induction-head construction
rows.value: Theorem 4.1 states that the conditional 1-gram model can be represented.
rows.note: The proof specifies first-layer attention to the previous position and second-layer matching on the current token, followed by copying the next-token values. This is a representation construction, not evidence that training finds it.
rows.check: This is an existence construction: the composed mechanism suffices. It does not show that training forms it. The paper credits a version of this result to Edelman et al. 2024.

source_check.locator_found: Theorem 4.1; Section 4; Appendix A, equations (7), (11), and (12).

rows.subject: 2-layer attention-only transformer with k heads in the first layer
rows.operation_detail: Constructed a k-head first layer that collects the preceding k positions, followed by a matching attention layer representing the conditional k-gram model.
rows.measure: Representation of the conditional k-gram model using a kth-order induction head
rows.value: Theorem 4.4 states that the conditional k-gram model can be represented.
rows.note: The construction explicitly matches the preceding k-symbol histories and averages the next-symbol values at matching positions.
rows.check: This is a k-head construction of a kth-order (long-prefix) induction head. That generalisation is not V1's [A][B]…[A]→[B] mechanism from a previous-token head.

rows.subject: Attention-only transformer with 1 head per layer
rows.operation_detail: Constructed a logarithmic-depth transformer that aggregates context across positions and uses a kth-order induction head to represent the conditional k-gram model.
rows.measure: Representation of the conditional k-gram model using induction-head attention
rows.value: Theorem 4.5 states that the conditional k-gram model can be represented.
rows.note: The construction expands the window of represented positions by combining information across layers; it is not a report of a trained model forming the mechanism.
rows.check: This is a log-depth construction of a kth-order induction head, a generalisation outside V1.

rows.subject: L-layer attention-only transformer with 1 head per layer
rows.operation_detail: Derived a conditional lower bound on representing a kth-order induction head under Assumption 6.2.

rows.measure: Whether the final-layer attention pattern can represent a kth-order induction head
rows.note: This is a conditional theoretical impossibility result, not an empirical failure.
rows.check: This conditional impossibility result concerns kth-order induction heads (k≥3), not the standard induction head named in V1.

rows.subject: 2-layer, 1-head transformer trained on an order-1 Markov process
rows.stage_stated: trained on an order-1 Markov process
rows.operation_detail: Measured the first-layer attention pattern across test sequences.
rows.measure: First-layer attention pattern across input sequences
rows.value: The text says attention focuses on the previous symbol for almost all indices and is largely independent of the input sequence.
rows.note: Figure 8 plots mean and standard deviation across sequences. This measures a previous-token component only; it does not demonstrate the full induction-head matching and copying behavior.
rows.check: Section 6.1 states the model is attention-only. It shows only the previous-token component; second-layer matching and copying were not measured.

labels.reason: R1 constructs previous-token attention followed by matching and copying. R7 observes the previous-token component after training. Support concerns the mechanism's sufficiency; training-induced formation of the complete circuit remains untested.

relation.reason: Theorem 4.1 constructs the composed V1 mechanism; Figure 8 independently examines its previous-token component in a trained model.

tranche.reason: Theoretical constructions and trained attention maps bear on V1 using a different method from the original training-dynamics measurements.

source_check.notes: Theorem 4.1 is an existence construction, credited in part to Edelman et al. 2024. Figure 4 uses standard transformers with MLPs and layer normalization; low task loss alone does not demonstrate induction heads.

statements.correction: arXiv:2407.17686: Figure 8; trained 2-layer, 1-head attention-only transformer; order-1 Markov process; 100 test sequences of length 128; first-layer attention concentrated on the previous symbol and largely input-independent; second-layer matching and copying untested.
statements.problem: The statement cites this study's R7 but omits arXiv:2407.17686 from its account. R7 cannot substantiate second-layer matching or copying; the explicit numerical claims concern other studies.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Explicit attention-only constructions in Theorems 4.1, 4.4, and 4.5
reader_labels.reason: The constructions represent conditional k-grams through matching histories and collecting the next-token values, using the induction-head mechanism (R1–R3).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Conditional lower bounds under Assumption 6.2 and the trained order-1 model measurement
reader_labels.reason: The bounds restrict which depth/head-count settings can represent kth-order induction heads, while the empirical attention result shows only a previous-token component, not the whole mechanism (R4–R7).
